page.purpose: Page background. The whole system sits on it.

surface-1.purpose: First raised surface: nav, cards, table headers, form fills.

surface-2.purpose: Second raised step: chips, secondary buttons, inset controls.

line-strong.purpose: Input borders, one step brighter than dividers.

ink-2.purpose: Secondary text: field labels, subtitles, table secondary cells.

ink-3.purpose: Muted hints, loading/empty states, ghost captions.

mark.purpose: The single accent: committed actions and checkbox accent.

shadows.name: flat
shadows.purpose: The system has no box-shadows. Depth is tonal stepping, 1px hairlines, and the black/40 note scrim.

motion.name: state-change
motion.value: time-based; Tailwind default transition on hover
motion.purpose: Hover state = one tonal step lighter. No keyframes, no entrance motion specified.

components.name: Quiet Primary Button
components.description: Row and page actions: Refresh, Settings, per-row Save. Soft graphite fill, ink label, hover one step lighter.
components.html: <button class="rounded bg-control px-3 py-1.5 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-control-hover">Refresh</button>

components.name: Committed Mark Button
components.description: The one committed action per surface (Setup Continue, Settings Save). Vermilion fill, page-colored label.
components.html: <button type="submit" class="rounded bg-mark px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-page hover:bg-mark-hover">Continue</button>

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Regenerate. Toned Iron fill, ink label, hover to soft graphite.
components.html: <button class="rounded bg-surface-2 px-3 py-1.5 text-sm text-ink hover:bg-control">Regenerate</button>

components.name: Field
components.description: Text, password, select, textarea. Carbon slate fill, field-edge border; focus shifts border to correction steel.
components.html: <input class="rounded border border-line-strong bg-surface-1 px-3 py-2 text-ink outline-none focus:border-focus">

components.name: Chip
components.html: motd

components.name: Status Card
components.description: Platform config status card with signal dot. Flat, hairline border.
components.html: GitHub

narrative.overview:
Releaser's dashboard is the desk where a release's voice is set before it ships. Like a newsroom's copy desk — where prose is shaped, checked, and released without ceremony — the interface is dark, calm, and entirely in service of the work: repositories, settings, and the machine that writes notes while everyone sleeps.

The system is editorial restraint rendered in graphite. It is monochrome by conviction: cool-lean charcoal surfaces on a near-black page, a cold-press paper text ramp, and exactly one proofing color — a desaturated vermilion used the way an editor uses a pen, for the single committed action and little else. Hierarchy arrives through weight, size, and tonal stepping, never through color or shadow. The dashboard is flat, quiet, and legible at a glance.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first, cool-lean graphite palette; near-black page (#0d0f13) with one- and two-step raised surfaces.
Color is signal: vermilion for the committed action, green/red strictly for platform status, nothing decorative.
Flat by default — depth comes from 1px hairline borders and tonal steps, never shadows.
Precise, restrained controls: 4px radius, weight-differentiated states, hover = one tonal step lighter.
System font stack; typography does hierarchy by weight and size, not by face.

rules.name: The Editor's Mark Rule
rules.body: The vermilion appears only for the committed action on a surface (Setup Continue, Settings Save), checkbox accent, and nothing else. Two vermilion elements on one screen is a copy error.

rules.name: The Signal-Only Color Rule
rules.body: Green and red mean status, never decoration. A page is monochrome until a platform reports configured, saved, or failed.

rules.name: The Ink-On-Mark Rule
rules.body: Text on vermilion buttons is Midnight Graphite (text-page), because the mark is a working surface, not a bright badge.

rules.name: The One-Face Rule
rules.body: No display type, no webfonts. If a hierarchy problem needs a new size or weight, use the existing stack. A second typeface is a redesign, not a tweak.

dos: Do keep the page on Midnight Graphite and raise surfaces only one or two tonal steps (Carbon Slate, Toned Iron).
Do use the vermilion mark for exactly one committed action per surface, plus the checkbox accent.
Do treat green/red strictly as status signal (config dots, Saved, errors).
Do prefer tonal separation and hairlines over shadows — flat is the system.
Do keep the 4px radius constant across controls, cards, chips, and inputs.
Do show hierarchy with weight, size, and tonal stepping within the system font stack.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue (teal, blue, purple) — the palette is graphite + vermilion + signal green/red.
Don't add box-shadows, gradients, or glass effects to lift anything.
Don't fall back to default Tailwind zinc classes; the bespoke graphite ramp is the only allowed neutral.
Don't use the vermilion as link color, decoration, or ambient fill — its rarity is the point.
Don't use white text on vermilion buttons; mark buttons carry Midnight Graphite labels.
Don't change the radius per component; variation in shape reads as error.
